questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

Some people are shipwrecked on a tropical island and allocate their time between gathering coconuts and fishing. Each individual is equally productive in collecting coconuts or catching fish. Which diagram represents the production possibility curve of this community?

options.A: B C D coconuts coconuts coconuts coconuts O O O O fish fish fish fish

questions.questionText: Which characteristic of money is most essential if it is to serve effectively as a store of value?

options.D: scarcity

questions.questionText: A worker can make 10 hats or 5 pairs of shoes in a day. In the market, three hats can be sold at the same price as two pairs of shoes. The worker should make

options.C: 4 hats and 3 pairs of shoes daily.
options.D: 6 hats and 2 pairs of shoes daily.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D D shows an individual’s initial demand curve for public transport.

The table shows the price elasticity of demand for four goods and services. price elasticity motorcycles –1.6 telephone calls –1.0 football tickets –0.3 light bulbs 0.0 If the price of each item increased by 1%, for which items would the total expenditure increase?

options.D: motorcycles only

Four firms supply the market. The market supply is 50 units at $20 and 100 units at $40. The table shows the market share of each firm at the two prices. Which firm does not have a normal upward-sloping supply curve? market share (%) market share (%) at $20 at $40
The price of a good doubles but firms are able to increase production by only 10%. This is an example of

options.D: market failure.

questions.questionText: In a market there is a surplus of a good. Which change would cause the market to come to an equilibrium?

options.D: an increase in supply

questions.questionText: The market for sugar is in equilibrium. A disease affects the sugar crop and newspapers report harmful health effects of consuming sugar. Which combination of changes in demand and supply matches these events? demand supply

options.D: rises rises

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a demand curve for journeys on a toll road. toll per journey ($) demand 1000 2000 number of journeys per day If there is a reduction in the toll from $5 to $3, what is the resulting increase in the daily consumer surplus?
What is an economic reason why hospitals are often built and funded by the government?

options.B: Hospitals are very expensive to build and run.
options.C: Hospitals cannot use price to allocate demand.
options.D: Hospital treatments may benefit many apart from those who use them.

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the costs and benefits in four markets.
Which statement about costs is correct?

options.D: Social cost affects all members of society equally.

questions.questionText: A government is considering building a high-speed rail link. Why would it not proceed with the project?

options.A: The external benefit is greater than the external cost.
options.B: The private cost is greater than the private benefit.
options.C: The social benefit is greater than the social cost.
options.D: The social cost is greater than the social benefit.

questions.questionText: The production of a product generates a negative externality that increases as output rises. Which form of government intervention in the market is most suitable to tackle this externality?

options.D: an ad valorem indirect tax

questions.questionText: The government places a maximum price P on an agricultural product. The supply and demand conditions for this product are shown in the diagram. S P price D O quantity What will be the outcome in the market for this product?

options.A: There will be an equilibrium price and output.
options.B: There will be a surplus of the product.
options.C: There will be higher than expected profits.
options.D: There will be shortages of the product.

questions.questionText: Country M specialises in the production of cars while country N specialises in the production of televisions. They then trade with each other. What is most likely to reduce the level of specialisation and trade?

options.A: There is rising productivity in the production of cars in M and televisions in N.
options.B: There is a change from fixed to floating exchange rates between M and N.
options.C: There is a decrease in the costs of transporting cars and televisions between M and N.
options.D: There is an increase in the mobility of factors of production within M and within N.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D is a country’s demand curve for an imported good. The country’s government imposes an import tariff equal to P P on the good. W C P C price x y P W z D O quantity Which areas measure the resulting loss in consumer surplus and the resulting gain in government revenue? loss in gain in consumer government surplus revenue

options.D: y z

questions.questionText: In the base year, which combination of export and import price changes will have the greatest effect on the country’s terms of trade? export prices import prices

options.D: no change increase by 2%

questions.questionText: The table shows selected balances from a country’s balance of payments accounts in 2012. $ billion trade in goods –20 trade in services +5 net income +8 net foreign transfers –4 net foreign loans –3 What was the country’s current account balance in 2012?

options.A: –$15 billion B –$14 billion C –$11 billion D –$7 billion

questions.questionText: The table shows the changing structure of employment (%) in four countries between 1980 and 2012. Which country did not follow the same trends as the other three countries between 1980 and 2012? 1980 2012 not not agriculture industry services agriculture industry services employed employed (%) (%) (%) (%) (%) (%) (%) (%)
Aggregate demand in an economy may decrease as a result of an increase in

options.D: investment expenditure.

questions.questionText: The table shows the CPI rate of inflation (%) in the US from 2006 to 2013. 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2.5% 4.1% 0.1% 2.7% 1.5% 3.0% 1.7% 2.0% What can be concluded from the figures about the period 2006 to 2013?

options.A: There was one year of constant prices.
options.B: There were three years of deflation.
options.C: There were only four years of inflation.
options.D: There were eight years of rising living costs.

questions.questionText: How might an increase in the general price level lead to a rise in real household expenditure?

options.A: by increasing the expectations of further price increases
options.B: by increasing the level of real household debts
options.C: by increasing the level of real wages
options.D: by increasing the spending on exports

questions.questionText: Between 2011 and 2013, high street retailers reported that expenditure on home-produced and imported goods was reduced. Consumers did not take out loans as the economy was in a recession. What is the likely result of this?

options.A: a decline in the deficit in the trade account
options.B: a decline in the level of savings
options.C: a decline in the terms of trade
options.D: a decline in unemployment

questions.questionText: What does not directly increase the supply of £ sterling on the world currency market?

options.A: lower interest rates in the United Kingdom
options.B: higher interest rates in the United States
options.C: an increase in investment opportunities for foreign capital in Latin America
options.D: an increase in sales of United Kingdom exports to the United States

questions.questionText: There is a depreciation in a country’s exchange rate. If wage costs remain unchanged, what would be the most likely consequence?

options.A: a fall in the rate of inflation
options.B: an increase in profits of manufacturing exporters
options.D: an outflow of foreign direct investment

questions.questionText: The currency of a small island economy floats against the US$. The island’s Government introduces foreign exchange control restrictions on its citizens. What is the likely effect on the international value of the island currency and of the US$? island currency US$ value value
